name: Hyperspell
one_liner: Confirmed live; tagline is now "A brain for your company" — connects enterprise data sources into a permission-aware knowledge graph agents query as a filesystem.

name: Memory Store
one_liner: Confirmed: "One shared memory for your teammates, and agents" — synthesizes Slack/Gmail/Granola transcripts into shared company memory plus self-updating "Briefs".

name: Hyper
one_liner: Confirmed: "The self-driving company brain" — aggregates email, Slack, docs, calendar and GitHub into a knowledge graph powering AI employees.

name: Cerenovus
one_liner: Confirmed live; positions as "Institutional intelligence and decision infrastructure" — markdown-based knowledge graph over docs/email/Slack that maps operations and infers inefficiencies.

name: Savant
one_liner: Confirmed: "The Operational Memory Layer" — captures undocumented procedures and decision logic, turning them into structured context and agent skills (legal entity Bledger, Inc.).

name: Glen
yc_batch: YC (company page exists; batch not stated on page)
one_liner: Confirmed: "Agents that get smarter as your company works" — institutional learning layer that pulls Claude Code/Codex/Cursor sessions plus Slack, GitHub, tickets and docs, and injects prior context into new agent runs.

name: GBrain
yc_batch: not YC (open-source project by YC CEO Garry Tan)
one_liner: Open-source long-term memory layer that turns plain Markdown into a self-assembling knowledge graph for agents; ~74 tools over MCP, hybrid vector+BM25 retrieval.

name: Colrows
one_liner: Author of the reference article; a semantic execution layer that compiles business definitions into governed SQL for enterprise AI — adjacent (semantic/metrics layer) rather than a document-memory company brain.

name: Sentra
one_liner: Governed org-wide memory layer with bi-temporal tracking (when a fact was recorded vs. when it was true), commitment tracking and contradiction detection; served to humans and agents over REST/MCP.

name: Gyld
one_liner: Confirmed: "Business context for your AI agents" — managed company brain that ingests Gmail, Slack, QuickBooks, Notion, Drive and exposes company knowledge as MCP servers.

name: Naboo
one_liner: Confirmed: "The Reasoning Layer for Enterprise AI Agents" — builds a queryable Decision Graph across tickets, PRs, code and chat; on-prem/VPC, RBAC, forward-deployed-agent delivery model.

name: Saphenia
one_liner: "Context graphs for agents" — teaches agents how an organization decides, aimed at high-regulation enterprise (financial services, pharma).

name: Modern Relay (Omnigraph)
one_liner: Confirmed: "Context infra that helps AI coordinate knowledge" — enterprise context graph plus open-source Omnigraph, a git-style versioned graph DB where agents branch/propose/merge knowledge; raised ~$3M led by Point Nine (Apr 2026).

name: Pensieve
one_liner: "Full company context for every AI agent" — connects Slack, Notion, Drive, GitHub into a living relational model of people/projects/decisions/customers; free, BYO model keys. (Site returned 403 to automated fetch but is live per Product Hunt.)

name: Compendium
one_liner: "Keeping your team, agents, and data on one page" — company brain where all agents share one memory, plus multiplayer sessions letting teammates drive one Claude together; aimed at AI-native startups.

name: Company Brain
one_liner: Confirmed but early access/waitlist only: lightweight MCP connector that loads persistent business context into Claude, ChatGPT and Copilot sessions.

name: Lore
one_liner: AI knowledge base / "AI intranet" positioned as an enterprise brain, with a native MCP server so Claude, ChatGPT and Cursor can query company knowledge; spun out of Brewster Consulting Group.

name: Coworker AI
one_liner: Positions as an "active company brain" — connects 50+ sources, verifies and re-checks facts, pushes approved updates with an audit trail.

name: Agently
one_liner: "Agently Brain" built continuously from uploaded docs, Slack, Gmail, HubSpot, Linear, GitHub and 25+ other sources.

name: Vectorize
one_liner: RAG/vector pipeline platform publishing "how to build a company brain for AI agents" — a build-it-yourself context pipeline rather than a packaged company brain.

name: Mem0
one_liner: Confirmed: "AI memory that persists across sessions and agents" — the category's most-cited memory layer (vector + graph + KV), but scoped per-user/per-agent rather than org-wide.

name: Zep (Graphiti)
one_liner: Confirmed: "Agent memory, at enterprise scale" — temporal knowledge graph (open-source Graphiti engine) with fact-validity windows and sub-200ms retrieval; supports user, agent, org and domain graphs.

name: Letta (formerly MemGPT)
yc_batch: not YC (no batch; YC participated as an investor in the $10M seed led by Felicis)
one_liner: Confirmed: "Machines that learn" — OS-inspired tiered memory (core/recall/archival) that the agent edits itself via tool calls; open source.

name: Supermemory
yc_batch: not YC (raised ~$2.6M seed co-led by Susa Ventures, Browder Capital, SF1.vc; angels incl. Jeff Dean, Dane Knecht)
one_liner: Confirmed: "The memory layer for AI agents" — context-engineering platform with enterprise APIs, MCP-native connectors (Gmail, Drive, Notion, GitHub, OneDrive) and a consumer second-brain app.

name: Cognee
yc_batch: not YC (backed by Pebblebed, Vermillion Cliffs, 42 Cap, Combination VC, Angel Invest; part of Berkeley Xcelerator)
one_liner: Confirmed: "Open Source Memory Platform for Agents" — the closest OSS analogue to a company brain, connecting Slack, GitHub and Linear into one queryable graph+vector memory.

name: Honcho (Plastic Labs)
one_liner: Open-source "reasoning-first" memory for stateful agents with a peer-centric model (users, agents, groups, projects all first-class); managed cloud at api.honcho.dev; strong 2026 benchmark results.

name: Graphlit
yc_batch: not YC (~$3.56M raised; investors incl. Feld Ventures, 8VC, Vectura Ventures)
one_liner: Confirmed live: positions directly as a "Context layer for AI agents" — managed ingestion/knowledge-graph API for unstructured content.

name: Papr
one_liner: Caution: the main site now reads "AI apps that run GTM work", so the company appears to have pivoted toward GTM agents; the memory product survives as open-source Papr Memory (MongoDB+Qdrant+Neo4j predictive memory layer).

name: Basic Memory
one_liner: Open-source local-first knowledge graph written in plain Markdown, exposed to Claude/other assistants over MCP (search_notes, read_note, write_note); individual/small-team scope rather than org-wide.

name: LangMem (LangChain)
one_liner: LangChain's open-source memory SDK for extracting, consolidating, updating and searching long-term memory inside LangGraph agents.

name: Evermind (EverOS)
one_liner: Local-first, Markdown-native, user-owned portable memory layer with self-evolving skills and multimodal ingestion; public beta April 2026. Note: also publishes its own "Mem0 alternatives" listicles, so treat its rankings as vendor content.

name: Maximem (Synap)
one_liner: Memory and context management for AI agents; markets Synap on latency (~15ms P50) and LongMemEval scores. Note: all comparison pages found are Maximem's own vendor-run content.

name: Hindsight
one_liner: Named repeatedly in 2026 memory round-ups as an institutional-memory system (what an agent did, what went wrong, what humans corrected) — closest adjacent to the company-brain thesis, but I could not confirm a primary marketing site.

name: Memvid
one_liner: Single-file memory layer combining lexical and semantic search for persistent agent context; founded 2025, Tennessee. Primary site not confirmed via fetch.

name: Cloudflare Agent Memory
one_liner: Managed agent memory service with typed memory categories (Facts/Events/Instructions/Tasks) and shared-profile support — a hyperscaler entering the memory layer.

name: OpenMemory MCP
one_liner: "Memory for your AI Tools" — MCP-server memory shared across AI clients; listed in Product Hunt's LLM Memory category.

name: MemSync
one_liner: "Unified Memory for all of your apps" — cross-app memory layer, Product Hunt LLM Memory category.

name: Actx0
one_liner: "Memory infrastructure for AI agents" — Product Hunt LLM Memory launch.

name: Memori
one_liner: "Persistent memory from agent trace, not just conversation" — distinctive angle of learning from execution traces rather than chat logs.

name: RoryPlans
one_liner: "A shared brain for your agents and team" — team-scoped shared memory, one of the few Product Hunt LLM-memory launches with an org rather than personal scope.

name: Atlaso
one_liner: "One memory for every AI you use" — cross-assistant personal memory layer; personal rather than company scope.

name: Liminary
one_liner: "Ground your AI in saved knowledge as you work" — knowledge-grounding memory layer, Product Hunt LLM Memory category.

name: screenpipe
one_liner: "AI that records your computer work to power agents" — capture-layer feeding agent memory; YC S26, adjacent input source rather than a company brain itself.

name: Glean
one_liner: The incumbent to beat: enterprise AI search indexing 100+ apps with generative Q&A; named in nearly every company-brain round-up as the query-time-retrieval alternative to write-time comprehension.

name: Sana (Sana Labs)
one_liner: "Superintelligence for work" — enterprise knowledge, search and learning platform positioned as an "enterprise brain"; now part of Workday.

name: Guru
one_liner: AI knowledge management platform with verification workflows to keep answers current; knowledge-base heritage rather than agent-facing context API.

name: Tettra
one_liner: Structured wiki with AI search and a Slack bot for small teams; wiki-first, included in company-brain round-ups as the lightweight option.

name: Notion AI
one_liner: AI answers grounded in Notion pages, databases and connected sources like Drive and Slack — workspace-native context, the default incumbent many teams already have.

name: Atlassian Intelligence (Confluence)
one_liner: AI search and summarization across Jira tickets and Confluence docs; incumbent context surface inside the Atlassian estate.

name: Granola
one_liner: Meeting intelligence that transcribes computer audio into structured summaries — a high-value input feed to company brains (Memory Store explicitly ingests it) rather than a competitor.

name: Contextual AI
one_liner: Context-engineering platform with RAG 2.0 and sentence-level attribution; enterprise grounding rather than persistent org memory.

name: Sema4.ai
one_liner: Enterprise AI agent platform with a semantic layer for natural-language access to enterprise data; agent-platform-first, context layer second.

name: LlamaIndex
one_liner: Open-source data framework for connecting custom data to LLMs with end-to-end RAG pipelines and memory modules — the build-your-own substrate under many company brains.

name: Dvina
one_liner: "Private AI that connects 120+ apps and your live databases" — private connected-context assistant, adjacent to the company-brain framing.

name: Zep AI
one_liner: "Agent memory, at enterprise scale." — builds temporal context graphs from chat history + business data with sub-200ms retrieval; open-source engine is Graphiti, product itself is now cloud-only. YC page tagline: "Agent Context Is Hard. We Fixed It."

name: Memobase
one_liner: "User Profile-Based Long-Term Memory for AI Chatbot Applications" — evolving user profiles plus timestamped event timeline, FastAPI/Postgres/Redis, Python/Node/Go SDKs, Apache-2.0. CAVEAT: memobase.io returned 404 to my fetches (bot-block or outage); GitHub repo is active (~2.9k stars, 467 commits) and lists memobase.io as the site.

name: Basic Memory (Basic Machines)
one_liner: "One place for your notes, decisions, and workflows. For you, your AI tools, and your team." — MCP server that builds a persistent knowledge graph from plain Markdown files on disk; local free, cloud $15/mo. Local-first, Obsidian-compatible.

name: Hindsight (Vectorize.io)
one_liner: "Agent Memory That Learns" — MIT-licensed retain/recall/reflect memory system with observations, mental models and knowledge pages; 25+ LLM providers, Python/Node/Go/CLI SDKs, self-host or Hindsight Cloud. NEW FIND, not on your seed list.

name: Memori (MemoriLabs / GibsonAI)
one_liner: "Agent-native memory infrastructure" — LLM-agnostic layer turning agent execution and conversation into structured persistent state; dual-mode (conscious working memory + auto DB search), runs on your existing Postgres/MySQL, deploys cloud/VPC/on-prem. NEW FIND.

name: memU (NevaMind-AI)
one_liner: "The memory harness for proactive AI agents — structured storage, intent capture, 10x token reduction" — agentic memory framework for 24/7 always-on agents, multimodal ingest, RAG + LLM retrieval; hosted at memu.so, OSS on GitHub. NEW FIND. (memu.so homepage is JS-rendered and returned no text to my fetcher; GitHub confirms.)

name: MIRIX
one_liner: "Advanced Memory System for LLM Agents" — multi-agent assistant that captures screen/visual data and converts it into structured multi-type memories for QA. NEW FIND; smaller/research-flavored, weakest commercial signal of the set.

name: Memories.ai
one_liner: "The multimodal memory infrastructure for AI" — video/visual memory: Video Intelligence API + Visual Search API, indexing footage by people, events and context. REAL and in the memory-infra space, but it is video memory, NOT a text company brain — adjacent rather than a direct CentralAgent competitor.

name: Wato (Wato Labs)
one_liner: "The control point for AI agents at work" — a shared, permissioned AI workspace giving agents shared memory, reusable published skills, connected MCP tools and living artifacts so work compounds across a team; works with Codex, Claude Code/Desktop, Cursor and other MCP environments.

name: Almanac
one_liner: "The agent with a company brain" — bets that the AI context layer takes the shape of a wiki: compiles Slack, Gmail, GitHub and Calendar into a self-updating, browsable wiki with every claim source-linked, which its always-on agent reads before acting. Founders Kushagra Chitkara, Rohan Sharma, Divit Sheth; waitlist stage.

name: Sylph
yc_batch: not YC (built by nao Labs, YC X25)
one_liner: Open-source company brain shipped as a Git repo you fork — hosts company context, builds skills and agents with self-learning, agent-agnostic across Claude Code, Codex and Cursor, no vendor lock-in. Built by Claire at nao Labs to run her own YC startup; the credible open-source/DIY substitute for a paid company brain.
evidence: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=48232533 (Show HN: Sylph – the open-source company brain behind my YC startup)

name: Slite
one_liner: Incumbent knowledge-base vendor repositioning as a "managed company brain" — pairs a human-verified knowledge base with an AI agent connected to team tools, so the brain stays in sync with reality for both humans and agents. Notable as the non-YC/incumbent flank of the category.
evidence: https://slite.com/learn/company-brain (Slite's own "What is a Company Brain" guide, naming Supermemory and GBrain alongside itself)

name: Mosaic
one_liner: "Shared memory for your team's agents" — syncs every coding-agent session (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor + 11 more) into one shared read-only drive preserving what was attempted, changed and why. Thesis directly overlaps company-brain: "the real unit isn't the agent, it's one shared context store every agent reads from and writes to." ~2,000 installs, 37 orgs syncing.

name: Graphify Labs
one_liner: On-device/on-prem knowledge graph engine giving humans and agents "one shared, always-current knowledge graph of your whole codebase, across every language and every repo, plus its docs and tickets"; adds formal PR verification. ~105K-108K GitHub stars (first YC company to cross 100K mid-batch); CEO Safi Shamsi authored "The Memory Layer." Codebase-scoped rather than whole-company.

name: Blume (blume.codes)
yc_batch: S26 (Summer 2026) — reported by one source, NOT confirmed on the company's own site or a YC profile
one_liner: Local desktop sidecar beside Claude Code, Codex and Cursor that clusters repeated corrections and frustration signals into durable rules, hooks and skills — agent memory formed from correction rather than ingestion. CAUTION: distinct from Blume Benefits (YC W24, health-insurance broker AI) which owns the ycombinator.com/companies/blume slug; treat the S26 batch claim as unverified.
evidence: https://blume.codes/ (fetched — live, no YC mention) ; https://www.producthunt.com/products/blume-codes ; YC S26 claim only from https://www.getreadyforagents.com/news/enterprise-context-memory-infrastructure-agents/

name: Letta
yc_batch: not YC as a batch company (YC participated as an investor)
one_liner: From the MemGPT team — treats the LLM as an operating system where the agent calls tools to page facts in and out of its own context window and rewrites its own memory; ~$10M seed. Domain not independently fetched in this sweep (commonly letta.com); verify before citing.

name: Poth Labs
one_liner: Vertical narrowing of the same idea — "the customer brain for your company": unifies Fireflies calls, Slack, support tickets, CRM notes, surveys and product analytics into an entity graph (customers, accounts, features, behaviors), then fills gaps with adaptive AI interviews. Customer-feedback scoped, not a general org brain — a wedge competitor rather than a head-on one.

name: Epicenter
one_liner: "AI brain for your plain text knowledge" — local-first, open-source, open-format assistant that lives in a folder on your machine and becomes the access point to everything you've written. PERSONAL second brain, not a multi-user company brain: no org permissioning or team ingestion, so it competes only on the DIY/individual flank.

name: Engram
one_liner: Learned memory layer that trains a compact, continuously-improving per-customer memory so models 'actually know your organization' — claims frontier-model parity at up to 100x fewer tokens. FUNDING: $98M launch/stealth-exit round at a $600M valuation, announced 23 Jun 2026, from General Catalyst, Kleiner Perkins, Sequoia, Factory, Modern, Amplify Partners, Neo; angels Assaf Rappaport (Wiz), Andrej Karpathy, Pieter Abbeel. Founded Oct 2025, SF, 13 employees. Founders Dan Biderman (CEO), Sabri Eyuboglu (CTO), Jessy Lin, Jack Morris, Scott Linderman, Chris Ré. Customers: Microsoft, Notion, Harvey. Largest round in the category by far.
evidence: https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/engram-launches-with-98m-to-build-ai-that-actually-knows-your-organization-302807126.html ; https://www.cnbc.com/2026/06/23/ai-memory-startup-focused-on-cutting-token-costs-raises-98-million.html ; https://www.calcalistech.com/ctechnews/article/skoqbrumze ; site fetched: https://engram.com (live, 'AI That Learns From You')

name: Jedify
one_liner: 'The Context Graph for Enterprise AI' — connects databases, warehouses, SaaS apps, BI tools and unstructured docs/meeting recordings via APIs into a 'Semantic Fusion' context graph capturing relationships across entities, data, people, permissions and customers, with access controls preserved. FUNDING: $24M Series A led by Norwest, announced 10 Jun 2026, with S Capital, Cerca Partners, Oceans Ventures and Snowflake Ventures (strategic); ~$33M total raised. New York. CEO/co-founder Assaf Henkin. 10-20 early customers incl. Kiteworks and The Weather Company. Claims 75% token reduction vs metadata approaches.
evidence: https://techcrunch.com/2026/06/10/jedify-raises-24m-to-help-companies-arm-ai-agents-with-context-on-their-business/ ; site fetched: https://www.jedify.com (live, 'Give agents full context. Not metadata.')

name: Naïve
yc_batch: YC (batch not specified in sources; YC participated in the Series A)
one_liner: Infrastructure API for 'autonomous companies' — incorporation, virtual cards, compute, serverless agent runtime, multi-agent orchestration AND a shared memory layer that accumulates company-wide information and hands each agent only the context it needs. FUNDING: $28.5M Series A led by Nexus Venture Partners, announced 6 Aug 2026, with Y Combinator, Zetta, Liquid 2, and angels Gokul Rajaram, Tim Zheng, JD Sherman, Gert Lanckriet, Robert Chatwani, Zachary Sim. Founders Sean Dorje and Dennis Zax. ADJACENT, NOT CORE: shared memory is one of four research pillars, not the product — include as a watch-item rather than a head-to-head competitor. Primary marketing URL not confirmed by fetch, so the TechCrunch source is given as the URL.

name: Tribal
one_liner: 'Metadata Fabric' ingests and maps the full metadata layer of an enterprise system of record — objects, automations, permissions, dependencies, business rules — so context-aware agents can be shipped into Salesforce, ServiceNow, SAP, NetSuite and Workday in days. FUNDING: $10M seed led by Team8 with DYDX Capital and enterprise-software angels, announced 20 May 2026. Founded 2024 by Yoav Kolodner (ex-VP Eng, Salesforce), Yakir Daniel (Spot.io→NetApp, Swordfish→Huawei), Lior Sidi (ex-AI lead, Wix). Israeli/US. NOTE: context is scoped to systems-of-record metadata rather than a general company brain; URL gotribal.ai reported by SiliconANGLE but not fetch-verified by me.

name: Zaro
one_liner: Shared memory / context layer for AI agents, positioning the company itself as the hub so 'every agent reads from and writes to it at once, like a document the whole team edits live' — explicitly so knowledge compounds for the customer, not the software vendor. FUNDING: $5.1M pre-seed led by Cherry Ventures, announced ~9-19 Jun 2026; angels Thomas Wolf (Hugging Face co-founder), Thomas Dohmke (ex-GitHub CEO), Mandeep Singh, Charlie Songhurst, and Convergence founders Marvin Purtorab and Andy Toulis. London, UK; founded 2025 by Michael Bajwa and Qian Zheng, both ex-Convergence (acquired by Salesforce). Site returned HTTP 403 to my fetcher but is confirmed live and real via investor and trade press.

name: Trace
one_liner: Builds a knowledge graph of a company from email, Slack, Airtable and similar tools, then turns high-level tasks into step-by-step workflows, delegating some steps to agents and others to humans with the right context attached; framed by founders as 'from prompt engineering to context engineering'. FUNDING: $3M seed announced 26 Feb 2026, led by Y Combinator with Zeno Ventures, Transpose Platform Management, Goodwater Capital, Formosa Capital, WeFunder; angels Benjamin Bryant, Kevin Moore. London, UK. Founders Tim Cherkasov (CEO) and Artur Romanov (CTO). Positions against Anthropic enterprise agents and Atlassian Jira agents.

name: Onyx
one_liner: Open-source, self-hostable enterprise search and AI platform combining search, multi-model chat, deep research and custom agents. FUNDING: $10M in one round from First Round Capital and Khosla Ventures. Relevant as the open-source, self-hosted alternative that data-sensitive buyers evaluate instead of a hosted company brain — a pricing and deployment-model threat rather than an architectural one.

name: Airia
one_liner: Enterprise AI security, orchestration and governance platform that in Jun 2026 launched a 'Context Engineering' product line — Graph RAG with customizable knowledge graphs, a Semantic Layer for domain vocabulary grounding, and a Knowledge MCP Server for multi-hop agentic retrieval. FUNDING: no round found in 2026 searches; founded 2024. Included because it shows governance/security platforms bolting on context-layer features as a wedge — a bundling threat to standalone company brains rather than a startup competitor.

name: Falconer
one_liner: "The source of truth for high-speed teams" — self-updating engineering docs grounded in the codebase, exposed to coding agents via Falconer MCP; markets itself as running "context engineering at company scale." Backed by BoxGroup and The General Partnership.

name: Sentra (Dynamis Labs)
one_liner: "The Company Brain for your team and AI agents" — a governed organizational memory layer capturing decisions and commitments with bi-temporal tracking, queryable via one API/MCP. Backed by a16z Speedrun and Together Fund. (Distinct from sentra.io, the data-security company.)

name: In Parallel
one_liner: "The Shared Context Layer for Enterprise AI" — joins meetings, captures decisions and commitments as they happen, and serves permission-scoped, cited org context to Claude/ChatGPT/Copilot over MCP (agents can also write back). Helsinki-based, EU-hosted, €29/user/mo.

name: Interloom
one_liner: Munich-based enterprise operations workspace that delegates work across teams and AI agents while building a context graph ("MemoryRank") of cases, decisions and outcomes — positioned as turning expert operational knowledge into permanent agent memory. €14.2M/$16.5M seed led by DN Capital.

name: Webair AI
one_liner: "The Company Brain for your business" — a private company brain reachable by SMS or web, built on its Cortyx routing-and-memory engine that layers business, personal and operational knowledge and acts as a privacy shim to model providers. NY-based; SMB/prosumer positioning rather than agent infrastructure.

name: Memori (Memori Labs)
one_liner: "Agent-native memory infrastructure" — an LLM-agnostic layer that turns agent execution traces (not just conversation) into structured, persistent state; markets a "company brain" use case.

name: xmemory
one_liner: "Schema-grounded agent-first memory engine" — structures memory on the write path with schemas, types, constraints and dedup so agent memory can be trusted like data infrastructure. London-based, $4M/£3M pre-seed led by Fly Ventures; closed beta.

name: ByteRover
one_liner: "Share the right context across your agents and team. You control what crosses." — local-first, file-based memory for coding agents with selective team sharing; claims >92% retrieval accuracy.

name: MemoryLake
one_liner: "The memory lake for every AI" — multimodal memory infrastructure storing conversations and documents with end-to-end encryption so agents keep persistent context across sessions; free tier plus premium plans.

name: Graphon AI
one_liner: "The Intelligence Infrastructure across physical and digital worlds" — a "pre-model intelligence layer" turning video, audio, images, docs and databases into persistent relational memory agents reason over at petabyte scale. SF-based, $8.3M seed led by Novera Ventures.

name: Atlan
one_liner: Data governance/catalog vendor now positioning its Enterprise Data Graph as the certified "context layer" agents read from (semantic definitions, lineage, access policy). Governance-first, so it competes on trust rather than on unstructured company knowledge.
